easy.def: A signal to start.
examples: The actor waited for her cue.
The nod was my cue.
The music is the cue.

more.def: A signal for someone to begin doing something, such as speaking in a play.
examples: The actor waited for her cue to enter.
Her nod was my cue to start singing.
The bell was the cue for lunch.

easy.def: A long stick used in pool.
examples: He chalked the cue.
The cue is long.
He hit the ball with the cue.

more.def: A long, thin stick that is used to hit the ball in a game such as pool.
examples: He chalked the tip of the cue.
She aimed the cue at the ball.
The cue hung on the wall.

easy.def: The end of a sleeve.
examples: The cuff is wet.
My shirt has a button on the cuff.
I rolled up my cuff.

more.def: The band at the end of a sleeve or the folded edge at the bottom of a pant leg.
examples: I rolled up the cuffs of my sleeves.
The cuff on his shirt had a button.
Mud stuck to the cuffs of his pants.

easy.def: The way of life of a group of people.
examples: Each culture has its own food.
We learned about another culture.
Music is part of culture.

more.def: The beliefs, customs, art and way of life shared by a group of people.
examples: Each culture has its own foods and holidays.
We read about the culture of ancient Egypt.
Art and music are part of every culture.

easy.def: A small bowl with a handle for drinking.
examples: Drink from the cup.
I want a cup of milk.
The cup is full.

more.def: A small container with a handle that you drink from.
examples: She poured a cup of hot chocolate.
He drank a cup of milk with lunch.
The cup fell and broke.

easy.def: A way to measure food.
examples: Add one cup of flour.
Use two cups of water.
I need a cup of sugar.

more.def: A unit used in cooking to measure how much of something there is.
examples: The recipe calls for one cup of flour.
Add two cups of water to the pot.
Measure a cup of rice.

easy.def: Something that makes an illness go away.
examples: There is a cure.
The medicine is a cure.
Rest is a cure.

more.def: A treatment or remedy that makes a sickness go away for good.
examples: Doctors found a cure for the disease.
Rest is a cure for a cold.
Honey is a cure for a sore throat.

easy.def: To make a sick person well.
examples: The medicine cured him.
The doctor cures sick people.
The treatment cured her cough.

more.def: To make a sick person well again.
examples: The medicine cured his cough.
A good rest cured her headache.
The doctor cured the dog's infection.

easy.def: Wanting to know or learn about things.
examples: The cat's curiosity got it into trouble.
Curiosity helped her learn.
Her curiosity grew.

more.def: A strong wish to learn or know about something.
examples: Curiosity led her to open the box.
The scientist's curiosity made her ask many questions.
The kitten's curiosity got it into trouble.

easy.def: Wanting to know more.
examples: The curious kitten looked in the box.
I am curious about what is in the bag.
The curious baby touches everything.

more.def: Eager to learn or find out about something.
examples: He was curious about how airplanes stay up in the sky.
Curious visitors gathered around the strange machine.
She was curious to know where the trail led.

easy.def: Water or air that moves in one direction.
examples: The river has a strong current.
A current carried the boat away.
The ocean current is warm.

more.def: A steady flow of water, air or electricity in one direction.
examples: The strong current carried the leaf downstream.
Warm ocean currents flow past the island.
Electric current runs through the wire.

easy.def: Happening now.
examples: The current month is May.
His current job is baker.
Who is the current teacher?

more.def: Happening or being used at the present time.
examples: The current mayor has held the job for six years.
She told us about the current weather.
What is your current address?

easy.def: Right now.
examples: I am currently reading a book.
She is currently at school.
The store is currently closed.

more.def: At the present time.
examples: I am currently reading a book about space.
The store is currently closed for repairs.
He is currently in third grade.

easy.def: A rude word, or a wish for bad luck.
examples: The witch put a curse on him.
It was a curse in the story.
The curse was broken.

more.def: A magic spell that brings bad luck, or a rude word said in anger.
examples: In the story, a witch put a curse on the castle.
The curse was broken at midnight.
The knight lifted the curse.

easy.def: To say rude words.
examples: Do not curse.
He cursed when he dropped it.
She never curses.

more.def: To use rude words, or to wish bad luck on someone.
examples: It is rude to curse in front of others.
He cursed when he stubbed his toe.
In the tale, the witch cursed the prince.

easy.def: A piece of cloth that hangs over a window.
examples: Close the curtain.
The curtain is blue.
The curtains are open.

more.def: A piece of cloth that hangs to cover a window or a stage.
examples: Close the curtains so the sun does not wake us.
The curtain rose and the play began.
The curtains in my room are blue.

easy.def: A usual way of doing something.
examples: It is a custom to shake hands.
That is a family custom.
The custom is old.

more.def: A way of doing something that people have done for a long time.
examples: It is a custom to give flowers on birthdays.
We have a family custom of walking on Sundays.
The custom began long ago.

easy.def: A person who buys things.
examples: The customer paid.
A customer came in.
The shop has many customers.

more.def: A person who buys goods or services from a shop or business.
examples: The customer paid for the loaf of bread.
A customer asked the clerk a question.
The bakery has many customers every morning.

easy.def: Special ways of doing things that a group follows.
examples: Every land has its own customs.
We learn about customs.
A custom of the holiday.

more.def: The traditional ways that a group of people do things.
examples: Every country has its own customs.
We learned about the customs of Japan.
Giving gifts is a custom on birthdays.

easy.def: The place where officials check bags at a border.
examples: We went through customs.
The customs officer looked at the bag.
The customs line was long.

more.def: The place at an airport or border where officials check what people bring into a country.
examples: We went through customs at the airport.
The customs officer checked our bags.
Officials at customs asked where we had traveled.

easy.def: To use something sharp to split or open.
examples: Cut the paper.
She cut the cake.
I cut the string.

more.def: To use a sharp tool to split, open, or take off a piece of something.
examples: Please cut the apple into four pieces.
He cut a long piece of string for the kite.
The barber cut my hair very short.

easy.def: A small hurt made by something sharp.
examples: I have a cut.
She has a cut on her hand.
A cut can sting.

more.def: An opening or injury made by something sharp.
examples: She had a small cut on her finger from the paper.
The nurse put a bandage on the cut.
He made a straight cut in the cloth.

easy.def: Sweet and fun to look at.
examples: The puppy is cute.
The kitten has cute ears.
Her hat is cute.

more.def: Pretty or sweet in a way that makes people smile.
examples: The kittens looked cute in their little hats.
What a cute baby!
She drew a cute cartoon of a smiling cloud.
